scenes.tts: A spike fires at one spot. How does it reach the far end, and why doesn't it come back?
scenes.visual: A long axon drawn left to right. One patch near the left end glows. The question appears above.
scenes.narration: A spike fires at one spot. How does it reach the far end, and why doesn't it come back?

scenes.tts: Inward current at the active patch spreads along the core of the axon. It brings the next stretch of membrane to threshold.
scenes.visual: Current loops flow from the glowing patch along the inside of the axon into the next patch, which brightens toward threshold.
scenes.narration: Inward current at the active patch spreads along the core of the axon. It brings the next stretch of membrane to threshold.

scenes.tts: That stretch fires, and its current spreads on to the next. The spike moves along, patch by patch.
scenes.visual: Patches light in sequence from left to right.
scenes.narration: That stretch fires, and its current spreads on to the next. The spike moves along, patch by patch.

scenes.tts: Here is a question. Current spreads both ways from the active patch. So why doesn't the spike turn back?
scenes.visual: Current loops shown flowing both forward and backward from the active patch. On screen: Pause. Why doesn't the spike turn back?
scenes.narration: Here is a question. Current spreads both ways from the active patch. So why doesn't the spike turn back?

scenes.visual: the question stays on screen

scenes.tts: The membrane just behind has just fired. Its sodium channels are inactivated. It is refractory, so it cannot be excited again.
scenes.visual: The patch behind the spike turns grey and is labelled refractory. Backward current reaches it and nothing happens.
scenes.narration: The membrane just behind has just fired. Its sodium channels are inactivated. It is refractory, so it cannot be excited again.

scenes.tts: The axon itself has no preferred direction. Stimulate the middle, and spikes travel both ways. A spike travels away from wherever it started.
scenes.visual: A stimulus electrode in the middle of the axon. Two spikes move out, one left and one right, each with a grey refractory wake.
scenes.narration: The axon itself has no preferred direction. Stimulate the middle, and spikes travel both ways. A spike travels away from wherever it started.

scenes.tts: Speed depends first on diameter. A wider axon has lower internal resistance, so current spreads farther before leaking away.
scenes.visual: A narrow and a wide axon side by side. Current reaches farther along the wide one before fading.
scenes.narration: Speed depends first on diameter. A wider axon has lower internal resistance, so current spreads farther before leaking away.

scenes.tts: Think of a wide pipe against a narrow, leaky one. Farther spread means a faster spike, which is why the squid giant axon is so wide.
scenes.visual: Water flows farther down a wide pipe than a narrow leaky one. On screen only: unmyelinated velocity rises roughly with the square root of diameter.
scenes.narration: Think of a wide pipe against a narrow, leaky one. Farther spread means a faster spike, which is why the squid giant axon is so wide.

scenes.tts: The other way to speed up is myelin, glial membrane wrapped around the axon.
scenes.visual: Glial wrapping forms around stretches of the axon, leaving short gaps.
scenes.narration: The other way to speed up is myelin, glial membrane wrapped around the axon.

scenes.tts: Picture a leaky garden hose wrapped in tape. Less current leaks out.
scenes.visual: A garden hose with leaks along it; tape wraps around it and the leaks stop.
scenes.narration: Picture a leaky garden hose wrapped in tape. Less current leaks out.

scenes.tts: Myelin also lowers capacitance. Think of a narrow water tank: the same pour raises its level more.
scenes.visual: A wide tank and a narrow tank receive the same steady pour; both levels rise while the water flows, the narrow one faster. Label: capacitance = tank width.
scenes.narration: Myelin also lowers capacitance. Think of a narrow water tank: the same pour raises its level more.

scenes.tts: With less capacitance, the same charge raises the voltage more. The voltage climbs as the charge arrives.
scenes.visual: The tanks become membrane patches: a voltage meter climbs during charging, faster for the myelinated (narrow) one. Label: less charge needed.
scenes.narration: With less capacitance, the same charge raises the voltage more. The voltage climbs as the charge arrives.

scenes.tts: So current from one gap reaches the next fast and strong. The gaps are nodes of Ranvier, where sodium channels regenerate the spike.
scenes.visual: The myelinated axon again. Nodes are labelled nodes of Ranvier, dense with sodium channel icons. Nodes light up in sequence.
scenes.narration: So current from one gap reaches the next fast and strong. The gaps are nodes of Ranvier, where sodium channels regenerate the spike.

scenes.tts: This is saltatory conduction, from the Latin for leap. Excitation skips the wrapped stretch. Current does not. It flows through the axon from node to node.
scenes.visual: Glow jumps node to node, while a steady current line flows continuously inside the axon beneath the myelin.
scenes.narration: This is saltatory conduction, from the Latin for leap. Excitation skips the wrapped stretch. Current does not. It flows through the axon from node to node.

scenes.tts: Speeds vary widely. In mammalian nerve, unmyelinated C fibres conduct at about walking pace. The largest myelinated fibres are roughly a hundred times faster.
scenes.visual: Velocity bar chart. Unmyelinated C fibres: about 0.6 to 2 m/s, with a walking figure. Largest myelinated fibres: about 70 to 120 m/s, with a fast train. Note: mammalian peripheral nerve; values depend on species and temperature.
scenes.narration: Speeds vary widely. In mammalian nerve, unmyelinated C fibres conduct at about walking pace. The largest myelinated fibres are roughly a hundred times faster.

scenes.tts: Now strip the myelin from one stretch. What happens to the spike?
scenes.visual: One internode loses its wrapping. On screen: Pause. Demyelinate one stretch: what happens?
scenes.narration: Now strip the myelin from one stretch. What happens to the spike?

scenes.visual: the question stays on screen

scenes.tts: The bare stretch leaks current and has more membrane to charge. The next node is reached late, or not at all. Conduction slows or blocks.
scenes.visual: Current leaks out of the bare stretch. The next node lights late in one run and not at all in another.
scenes.narration: The bare stretch leaks current and has more membrane to charge. The next node is reached late, or not at all. Conduction slows or blocks.

scenes.tts: It does not always block. In some fibres the bare stretch develops sodium and potassium currents of its own. Then it conducts slowly and continuously.
scenes.visual: A glow creeps smoothly and slowly along the bare stretch, as along an unmyelinated axon.
scenes.narration: It does not always block. In some fibres the bare stretch develops sodium and potassium currents of its own. Then it conducts slowly and continuously.

scenes.tts: Back to the puzzles. Overshoot: sodium briefly pulls the balance point above zero. Threshold: sodium feedback sustains itself. All-or-none: brief pushes from rest give spikes of about the same size.
scenes.visual: The checklist from chapter 1 returns. Each item ticks as its answer appears.
scenes.narration: Back to the puzzles. Overshoot: sodium briefly pulls the balance point above zero. Threshold: sodium feedback sustains itself. All-or-none: brief pushes from rest give spikes of about the same size.

scenes.tts: Refractoriness: inactivated sodium channels need time to recover. Travel: current spreads ahead, and refractory membrane behind blocks the way back.
scenes.visual: The last two items tick.
scenes.narration: Refractoriness: inactivated sodium channels need time to recover. Travel: current spreads ahead, and refractory membrane behind blocks the way back.

scenes.tts: Spread ahead, refractory behind. Wider and myelinated means faster.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card on screen: Spread ahead, refractory behind. Wider and myelinated means faster.
scenes.narration: Spread ahead, refractory behind. Wider and myelinated means faster.
